summary: Under Disposición 002-2026, in force since 16 February 2026, Nicaragua sorts nationalities into two categories. Category A — nationalities including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Saudi Arabia and Qatar — needs no visa; the UK Foreign Office says British visitors can stay up to 90 days and must pay a 10 US dollar arrival tax in cash. Category C — nationalities including Mexico, Colombia, New Zealand, China, India and Cuba — needs a "consulted" visa, which Nicaragua's immigration authority says is applied for, paid for and downloaded online.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must pay an arrival tax of 10 US dollars in cash, and that the US dollar is the only foreign currency freely exchangeable in Nicaragua.

The UK Foreign Office says the 90-day visa-free period for Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras starts when you enter any of them and does not restart when you cross between them, and that if you overstay you may get a fine.

Canada's travel advice cites UN reports that the authorities prevent certain people from entering or leaving Nicaragua for political reasons and arbitrarily search personal phones and computers for anti-government content. Both Canada and the UK Foreign Office say political activity by foreigners is illegal and can lead to detention or deportation.

The UK Foreign Office says several volcanoes are active, in particular San Cristóbal, Masaya, Cerro Negro, Telica and Concepción on Ometepe Island, and advises not to hike on volcanoes without an experienced guide. It says the hurricane season normally runs from June to November.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nicaragua?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Under Disposición 002-2026, in force since 16 February 2026, Nicaragua has two categories. Category A — nationalities including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Saudi Arabia and Qatar — needs no visa. Category C — nationalities including Mexico, Colombia, New Zealand, China, India and Cuba — needs a "consulted" visa, which Nicaragua's immigration authority says is applied for, paid for and downloaded online. The UK Foreign Office says British visitors can stay up to 90 days without a visa, and Canada says the same for Canadians.

faq.question: Is there an arrival fee for Nicaragua?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you must pay an arrival tax of 10 US dollars in cash, and that there is also a departure tax of 35 US dollars, normally included in the price of your air ticket.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Nicaragua?
faq.answer: No readable official Nicaraguan page states the stay. The UK Foreign Office says British visitors can stay up to 90 days without a visa, that the 90-day period is shared with El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras under the CA-4 agreement, and that you can extend your stay by up to 30 days by paying a fee before the 90 days expire. Canada says Canadians need no tourist visa for stays of up to 90 days. No official source we could read states the fee.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 agreement affect my trip?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the 90-day visa-free period for El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua starts when you enter any of the four and does not restart when you cross borders between them; you still go through immigration checks at each border.

faq.question: What is a "consulted" visa (visa consultada)?
faq.answer: It is the visa for the nationalities in Category C under Disposición 002-2026, including Mexico, Colombia, China, India and Cuba (ordinary passports). Nicaragua's immigration authority (DGME) says in a February 2026 leaflet that you apply online at tramitesconsulares.mint.gob.ni, that immigration reviews the application, that you pay online by VISA or Mastercard once notified, and that you then download the approved visa; it says you do not have to go to a consulate. DGME's visa page still describes the visa as granted through Nicaragua's diplomatic and consular representations. That page asks for a passport valid for at least six months, a letter requesting the visa, a police certificate and a notarized undertaking to cover your costs.

faq.question: Is Nicaragua safe to visit right now?
faq.answer: Canada says to exercise a high degree of caution because of the political situation, the potential for civil unrest and crime. The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal for foreigners to take part in any political activity, including protests, and that you can be arrested, detained or deported for it.
